purpose: Lets an independent test suite written against an earlier recipes schema be pointed at the current one without hiding its original results. It maps fields and reason codes; it does not change, rerun or reinterpret any Codex test. Codex reported (event 115, review 08af19f, not available here) 79 original checks: 33 reached (11 pass, 22 schema mismatches), 46 not executed; those numbers are Codex's and are not reproduced or altered by the author.

versions.why: R02-A/R02-B: blacklist guards failed open; allow-lists, real-date periods, dated FX, item definitions, CFO placement policy, composed FCF
R02-C lease semantics (reported vs derived CFO, lease placement per issuer, single deduction), R02-D input-shape validation, R02-E finite arithmetic

v1_to_v2.generic_failure_conditions: removed; generic checks are a fixed ordered list (see check_order) implemented by the evaluator, not data
v1_to_v2.recipes[].failure_conditions (eq/neq/mis: kept for metric-specific rules only, ops reduced to always/and/eq/neq_path/not_in; definitional checks moved to required_definitions
v1_to_v2.recipes[].required_definitions: new: {meta_field: [allowed values]}; missing -> definition_missing:<f>, unlisted -> definition_not_accepted:<f>
v1_to_v2.recipes[].item_definitions: new: {item: definition_id}; each used item needs meta.item_definitions[item] equal to it
v1_to_v2.recipes[].outputs[].selector / cases: replaced by outputs[].terms [{expr, sign, when?}] (ratio outputs: numerator/denominator term lists)
v1_to_v2.examples[].meta.period.start: now required (period validated by kind, real dates, order, duration)
v1_to_v2.examples[].meta.fx.window_start / window: now required for non-USD monetary cells
v1_to_v2.examples[].meta.capex_line_includes_acqu: no longer read; replaced by capex_acquisitions_classification and investments_classification (allow-list: separately_disclosed)

v2_to_v3.recipes[].required_definitions_by_basis: new: {IFRS|US_GAAP: {meta_field: [allowed]}}; M05 records where each lease cash flow sits in the published statement
v2_to_v3.M05 outputs: cfo_norm (v2) replaced by two outputs: reported_cfo (role reported_not_comparable: the published figure, converted only) and cfo_after_lease_payments (role derived_comparable: all lease payments and interest deducted once)
v2_to_v3.M05 meta (IFRS): new required: lease_principal_classification [financing], lease_interest_classification [operating|financing] (must equal interest_paid_classification)
v2_to_v3.M07 outputs[0].terms: ref:M05.cfo_norm -> ref:M05.cfo_after_lease_payments (never reported_cfo); no lease term in FCF
v2_to_v3.items: any item not defined by the recipe or its dependencies -> item_not_recognised:<item>; forbidden items of dependencies apply to the dependant

v1 -> v2/v3.period_end_missing: period_date_invalid (end or start missing/invalid) | period_missing (no period object)
v1 -> v2/v3.fx_rate_type_mismatch: fx_rate_type_mismatch (plus new fx_window_mismatch, fx_date_mismatch, fx_rate_invalid, fx_unexpected_for_usd, currency_not_supported)
v1 -> v2/v3.no_recipe_for_case: definition_not_accepted:<field> or a basis-consistency code (e.g. inventory_method_inconsistent_with_basis)
v1 -> v2/v3.gas_factor_policy_missing: policy_missing:gas_scf_per_boe (policy_invalid:gas_scf_per_boe when not a positive finite number)

new in v3.input_malformed:example|meta|items|polic: R02-D: wrong type, null or missing structure; checked before any property is read
new in v3.non_finite_result: R02-E: any intermediate or final value (sum, difference, product, quotient, FX conversion, rounding) not finite; division by zero
new in v3.item_not_recognised:<item>: item outside the recipe and its dependencies (prevents an unlisted second deduction)
new in v3.lease_interest_classification_differs_fr: R02-C: IFRS lease interest placed apart from other interest paid
new in v3.definition_missing|definition_not_accept: R02-C: lease placement not recorded or without a recipe
R02-C: capex must exclude lease payments and right-of-use additions

evaluator_interface.v1: evaluate(recipe, example) -> {status, reason} | {status, values}; examples[].expected compared
evaluator_interface.v2/v3: evaluate(recipe_id, example) and evaluate_pair(recipe_id, a, b); values are keyed by output key; pair values {a: {...}, b: {...}}; an unknown recipe id throws (caller fault); malformed data never throws
evaluator_interface.reference implementations: tools/recipes.py (generator, --evaluate <cases.json> for batch parity) and checks/evaluator.ts (independent); both must agree on every case

how_to_point_an_earlier_suite_at_v3: Keep the original assertions and results as recorded; run them against v3 separately and report mismatches as schema mismatches, not as passes.

For a v1/v2 example, add meta.period.start, FX window/date, meta.item_definitions from the recipe, and the allow-listed definitions the case is about; do not add fields that would make a must-fail case pass.
Map expected reason codes with reason_codes above; codes now carry the field or item after a colon.
For M05/M07 compare cfo_after_lease_payments (not reported_cfo) and fcf_rebuilt; reported_cfo is the published figure and is expected to differ between classifications.

precision_policy_event_117.rule: Every numeric input (items, FX rate, positive policy factors) and every intermediate and final value must lie within the IEEE-754 safe-integer range |v| <= 9007199254740991 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); otherwise NOT_COMPARABLE. Inputs: unsafe_integer_precision:<item> | :fx.rate | :policy.<key>; intermediates and results: unsafe_integer_precision. Non-finite values keep non_finite_result; values beyond the double range keep item_not_numeric / fx_rate_invalid / policy_invalid (event 116).
precision_policy_event_117.python: json.loads keeps integers exact; the bound is compared on the original int before any float conversion (safe_input), so no rounding happens before the check.
precision_policy_event_117.typescript: JSON.parse has already rounded the source text. The bound still rejects every integer text above the safe range, because any such text parses to at least 2**53; fractional digits lost inside the range cannot be detected after parsing (a raw-text check would be needed, not implemented).
precision_policy_event_117.not_used: No BigInt or Decimal in either evaluator; exact integers are used only in test references.

reason_code_changes_from_event_116.inputs above the safe range but within t: previously accepted, or non_finite_result after overflow -> now unsafe_integer_precision:<input>

precision_policy_event_118.rule: No financial result is accepted unless it equals, at the reported precision, the value the decimal precision policy allows for the raw input. Raw input enters through evaluate_raw / evaluateRaw, which keep every JSON number as its source text until it is checked; Python and TypeScript apply the same policy and agreement between them is not taken as proof.

decimal_places.items (amounts and quantities): at most 6 written decimal places (trailing zeros do not count; exponent form is expanded: 1.25e2 has 0, 1e-7 has 7)
decimal_places.results: reported and verified at 6 decimals, half-to-even on the exact value; ratios (gearing, margins) are results

precision_policy_event_118.unit_scale: Amounts are read in the unit and scale the example declares (unchanged); the policy does not rescale. FX converts by dividing by the rate (unchanged). Conversion factors are policy inputs.
precision_policy_event_118.safe_conversion: A lexeme becomes a double only if it has no more places than allowed and the double, read back at the written places, is exactly the written value; the exact value is kept beside the double for verification.

rejection_codes.decimal_places_exceed_policy:<item> | :p: more written places than the policy allows
rejection_codes.unsafe_decimal_precision:<item> | :polic: the nearest double does not name the written value (e.g. 9007199254740990.9 reads 9007199254740991)
rejection_codes.precision_not_guaranteed:<output>: the reported number, read as printed, differs from the exact result at 6 decimals (intermediate or result too fine for its double, e.g. 4503599627370495.5 + 0.75, or 123456789012.35 - 123456789011.5)
rejection_codes.input_malformed:json: text is not strict JSON (NaN, Infinity, trailing comma, comment, leading zero, truncation) or nests deeper than 64 levels
rejection_codes.unchanged: magnitudes of 1e16 and above keep the event 116/117 codes (unsafe_integer_precision[:<input>], item_not_numeric, fx_rate_invalid, policy_invalid); non_finite_result unchanged

precision_policy_event_118.no_silent_rounding: No input is rounded to fit the policy and no result is passed on rounded beyond the stated 6 decimals; a value that cannot be guaranteed is NOT_COMPARABLE with one of the codes above.
precision_policy_event_118.verification_only: Exact rationals (Python fractions.Fraction; TypeScript BigInt numerator/denominator) are used only to verify; reported values are still computed in doubles by the unchanged formulas. No new financial engine.
precision_policy_event_118.trust_boundary: evaluate(recipe, example) on an already parsed object cannot see digits an earlier parser (JSON.parse, json.loads to float) has already lost: it reads each double as its shortest printed decimal and still verifies every intermediate and result exactly. External data must enter through evaluate_raw / evaluateRaw; the object path is for data built in code (generator, tests).
precision_policy_event_118.interfaces: python tools/recipes.py --evaluate-raw <file>: [{recipe, text}] -> results; checks/evaluator.ts makeEvaluator(doc).evaluateRaw(id, text). evaluate / evaluate_pair / --evaluate unchanged in signature.
precision_policy_event_118.typescript_display_rounding: checks/evaluator.ts now rounds the reported double half-to-even exactly at 6 places (as Python round(v, 6) does) instead of Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6, which rounded half-up after an inexact product and decided exact ties (e.g. 0.000001 / 2) differently from Python. Values of 1e15 and above are still reported unrounded.
precision_policy_event_118.reason_code_changes_from_event_117: none for existing cases: all 738 earlier tests pass with unchanged expectations; the new codes appear only for raw-path inputs or for results the exact check rejects. COMPARABILITY-RECIPES.json is unchanged.
